summary.text: Participant 6 was a 66-year-old male with less than a high school education and prior VR use who was enrolled less than one week after a below-knee amputation with a diabetic indication. He had phantom limb pain at enrollment, deep vein thrombosis, chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, type 1 diabetes mellitus, peripheral vascular disease and hypertension.

He completed no VR GMI stage and had zero sessions. The recorded reasons were difficulties with control manipulation during left/right discrimination and discharge before troubleshooting could occur. He reported that he could not meaningfully assign a numerical value to his experience.

article_limitations: Case series of six participants whose individual data come only from Tables 1 to 3 and a few named-participant sentences; many results, usability and discussion statements are cohort-level or refer to unnamed participants and are not assigned.
Table 1 IDs 1 to 6 are treated as the same participants as P1 to P6 in the text and Tables 2 and 3 (text defines Participant 1 as P1); this mapping is not printed in Table 1 itself.
Text and Figure 3 disagree on which participant gave the low helpful rating and the 70% helpful rating; Figure 3 labels P2 to P5 only.
P4 is male in Table 1 and in the NRS paragraph but referred to with "her" in the satisfaction paragraph.
Text states −5-point session 2 decreases for P5, whereas Table 3 cells differ by 4 points.
Participant age is a bare number in Table 1 with no printed unit.
Analgesic regimens during VR GMI sessions were not systematically recorded by the authors; no medications beyond prior chemotherapy for P1 are documented.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the actual images are inspected in the separate visual target.

In the satisfaction paragraph the ratings attributed to P1 (low helpful), P2 (70% helpful) and P4 ("her") resemble the Figure 3 series P2, P3 and P5 and Table 1 participant 5 (female); a participant-numbering offset is possible but not stated, so those text statements are quarantined or left as written and never reassigned.
